claude.sample_unit: head and neck cancer cases (institutional external test set)

links.outcome: Auto-segmentation performance on local clinical data versus challenge performance
links.effect: Significant performance degradation on local cases; GTVp DSC 0.68, GTVn DSC 0.66, HD95 16.0 mm; FP errors in 5 GTVp and 12 GTVn cases.
links.quote: In our study, we observed significant performance degradation for GTVp and GTVn in independent clinical cases, mainly due to the high incidence of FPs and FNs in DLAS.

links.outcome: LLM extraction accuracy of tumor counts under basic versus refined prompt
links.effect: Prompt1 gave 47 primary tumors and 117 LNs; prompt2 gave 40 and 106 versus RadOnc 40 and 111, matching better.
links.quote: The results of prompt2 matched better those of the RadOncs.

links.outcome: Comparison of GPT-4 versus Llama-3-8B for tumor information extraction from reports
links.effect: GPT-4 extracted 40 primary tumors and 106 LNs vs RadOnc 40/111; Llama-3-8B gave 48 primary tumors and 127 LNs with extra false positives; Llama-3 inferior.
links.quote: Our study found that Llama-3 is inferior to the GPT-4 model in terms of tumor information extraction.

links.outcome: LLM misclassification of benign findings as malignant tumors in radiology reports
links.effect: GPT-4 misclassified suspected goiter and symmetric tonsil enhancement as tumor out of the box; prompt engineering improved accuracy.
links.quote: For example, in one instance, the report mentioned “symmetric enhancement in the tonsil region”, which GPT-4 incorrectly categorized as malignant primary tumor.

unlisted_practices: Using radiology report content extracted by LLM to rule out false-positive AI segmentation contours
Prompt engineering to emphasize impression section for LLM report extraction

links.effect: HECKTOR reported top DSCs 0.788/0.776; local baseline DSCs were 0.68 for GTVp and 0.66 for GTVn.
links.quote: The contouring agreement, as reflected by the DSC and HD95 metrics, remained inferior to the performance reported in the HECKTOR challenge, even after applying the FP ruling-out approach.

links.effect: On 44 local cases, 5 GTVp and 12 GTVn cases contained FP errors; eight GTVn FN errors were also found.
links.quote: Out of 44 cases, 5 and 12 cases contained FP errors for GTVp and GTVn, respectively.

links.effect: FP errors improved from 17/111 to 0/111 for GTVn and 5/40 to 0/40 for GTVp; precision reached 1.0.
links.quote: The ruling-out process successfully removed all FPs for both GTVp (5) and GTVn (17), achieving a perfect precision of 1.0.

links.effect: Before report-based ruling out, FP errors were 17/111 GTVn and 5/40 GTVp; FN errors were 8/111 GTVn and 0/40 GTVp.
links.quote: However, eight FN errors remained for 111 GTVn instances.

unlisted_practices: Prompt engineering that instructs the LLM to use the radiology report impression paragraph to classify findings as primary tumors or lymph nodes.

links.outcome: auto-segmentation performance degradation on local clinical data
links.effect: DLAS model achieved an average DSC of 0.68 for GTVp and 0.66 for GTVn, with false-positive errors in 5 and 12 of 44 cases, respectively.
links.quote: In our study, we observed significant performance degradation for GTVp and GTVn in independent clinical cases, mainly due to the high incidence of FPs and FNs in DLAS.

unlisted_practices: Automated post-processing verification of image auto-segmentation contours against LLM-extracted radiology report findings to rule out false positives

screen.practice: LLM-based report cross-check to rule out false-positive auto-segmentations
screen.reason: Evaluates using an LLM to cross-reference auto-segmentation contours against radiology reports as an automated verification/filtering safeguard to eliminate false-positive segmentations.
